answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a proof-of-participation mechanism to resist Sybil attacks. Each agent generates a unique, periodic pulse of cryptographic signatures, broadcasting its identity to the network at dawn of each epoch. To prevent fake identities, agents must demonstrate persistent, concurrent participation, validated by violet-hued, computationally intensive puzzles that verify liveness and resource commitment, costing an attacker substantial computational power and energy to create and maintain multiple pseudonyms.
